questions.q: The three main types of thinking in psychology include the following except
questions.explanation: In this course the three main types of thinking are symbolic, creative and divergent thinking, so convergent is the option left out.
questions.flag: Ambiguous: convergent and divergent thinking are usually presented as a classic pair, so 'convergent' being excluded depends on the course's specific list (symbolic, creative, divergent).

questions.q: Young children engaging in imaginative play often engage in ___ thinking.
questions.explanation: Imaginative (pretend) play uses one thing to stand for another, such as a stick as a horse, which is symbolic thinking. Piaget linked this symbolic function to the preoperational stage.

questions.q: Which of the following is a way in which we think?
questions.explanation: We think using verbal symbols (words), mathematical symbols, and also gestures, movements and images. Since all are ways of thinking, all of the given is correct.

questions.q: People experience the ___ experience when they find the solution to a problem suddenly that had been in their mind for hours or days, late.
questions.explanation: The 'aha' experience is the sudden insight when a solution to a problem appears after it has been in mind for some time. Kohler's insight learning studies describe this.

questions.q: ___ knowledge refers to knowledge of terminology and specific details.
questions.explanation: In Bloom's revised taxonomy, factual knowledge covers basic elements such as terminology and specific details. Conceptual knowledge covers relationships and theories, and procedural knowledge covers how to do things.

questions.q: Which of the following is not true about metacognition?
options: allows people to be dependent on others for their learning
often referred to as "thinking about thinking"
is crucial for efficient independent learning because it fosters self-reflection
is a regulatory system that helps a person understand and control his or her own cognitive performance
questions.explanation: Metacognition is thinking about thinking, a regulatory system that supports self-reflection and independent learning. It makes learners less, not more, dependent on others.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an effective way to develop reflective thinking?
questions.explanation: Asking questions, self-questioning and negotiated learning all encourage reflection. Avoiding reflective discussions prevents reflective thinking, so it is not an effective way.

questions.q: Which of the following is not true about creative thinking?
options: It is the ability to consider something in a new way
It is not a skill anybody can develop
It is the process of nurturing our imagination
It is all about developing innovative solutions to problems.
It requires a compilation of analytical, problem-solving, organizational and communication skills
questions.explanation: Creative thinking is a skill that can be developed and improved by anyone through practice. The other statements correctly describe creative thinking.

questions.q: The ___ stage of the creative thinking process refers to the "eureka" moment.
questions.explanation: In Wallas's model of creativity (preparation, incubation, illumination/insight, verification), the insight or illumination stage is the sudden 'eureka' moment when the idea appears.

questions.q: In a concept map, two nodes connected with a labeled arrow are called a
questions.explanation: In a concept map, two concepts (nodes) joined by a labeled linking arrow form a proposition, a meaningful statement. 'Preposition' is a grammatical term and a tempting look-alike.
